name: Honeybadger
summary: Honeybadger tracks errors with uptime checks and logs in one plan. The free Developer plan has 5,000 errors for one user. Team is $26 a month for 50,000 errors and unlimited users, and Business at $80 keeps error data 180 days.

facts.text: By default Honeybadger resolves all errors in a project when a deployment is reported, so recurring errors raise new alerts.
Errors are grouped by file name, method name, line number, class name and component, and a custom fingerprint can override the grouping.
Customers choose to store data in the United States or the European Union.
Error processing continues up to 125% of the monthly quota and then stops until the month ends.
A before_notify callback can drop a notice that contains sensitive data, and request.filter_keys defaults to password and password_confirmation.

plans.name: Developer
plans.notes: 1 user, 5,000 errors a month, 15-day error retention

plans.name: Team
plans.notes: 50,000 errors a month, unlimited users, 90-day error retention. The page also shows $286 a year

plans.name: Business
plans.notes: 50,000 errors a month, unlimited teams, 180-day error retention. The page also shows $880 a year

hiddenCosts: Optional overage billing charges $0.0003 per notification on Team and $0.0006 on Business above the quota.
Logging and performance tiers raise the price and set how long Insights data is kept.

security.ssoPlan: Not confirmed; the page lists SAML and custom sign-in without a plan
